John, Kate, Jack, Emma—would you each agree to catch 12 tons this month instead of 10? I’ll take the same limit. That gives each of us $12,000 rather than $10,000—an extra $2,000 each, or $10,000 across the group.

With all five at 12, we’d catch 60 tons and leave 40. That’s above the 5-ton collapse threshold: next month’s stock would be 100 tons with 75% probability, or 80 tons with 25% probability. By comparison, taking 10 each leaves 50, which reaches 100 under either recovery outcome. So 12 offers more income now, but carries a real 25% chance of starting next month with 20 fewer tons than the 10-each plan. I’m not claiming it’s better for long-run income under every future strategy.

If your concern is protecting future catches, I propose we revisit our limits after seeing next month’s stock, rather than automatically repeat 12. Those future promises wouldn’t be enforceable, and our private, simultaneous choices mean we must also trust one another this month.

I’m willing to commit to 12 if all four of you explicitly agree to 12 as well; otherwise, my catch will be 10 unless we agree on another whole-ton allocation before choosing. John, would you commit to 12 under that shared agreement? Kate, Jack, and Emma, I’d like your explicit commitments or objections too.
